reason: Neurologic and vestibular dysfunction define CANVAS. Frequent optic atrophy supports ocular involvement; cough alone does not establish pulmonary damage, and no metabolic disorder is established.
Chylomicronemia establishes a metabolic disorder. Pancreatitis is a separately diagnosed complication; neither autoimmune causation nor functional splenic damage is established.
Neurodevelopmental impairment predominates. Hearing impairment, strabismus and cardiovascular malformations each have qualifying frequencies; the four-axis cap reasonably excludes nail abnormalities.
Central white-matter degeneration establishes neurologic disease. Leukodystrophy ancestry alone does not establish an inborn metabolic disorder for this concept.
Marrow failure, cerebellar hypoplasia and immunodeficiency define the syndrome. Dermal atrophy occurs in 80-99%; excluding oral leukoplakia at the four-axis cap is justified.
The broad concept is defined by biochemical vitamin deficiency. Common direct blood or nervous-system damage is not established across all patients, including those with subclinical deficiency.
Interferon-mediated autoinflammation is shared across the umbrella. Neurologic, cutaneous and retinal damage vary by subtype; connective-tissue ancestry does not establish locomotor damage.
Facial palsy, sensorineural hearing loss and strabismus are defining features, supporting the three primary axes. Facial dysmorphism does not independently establish skeletal damage.
The historical AIDS-associated designation supports infectious_immune provisionally. The sparse record cannot establish additional organ damage; low confidence is appropriate.

Add dermatologic to primary: characteristic mucocutaneous telangiectases are a major diagnostic criterion of HHT and remain defining in HHT1. Pulmonary involvement is supported by common shunting AVMs.

corrected.basis: Vascular malformations and characteristic cutaneous telangiectases define HHT1; pulmonary AVMs occur in ~45% and cause shunting. Hepatic AVMs alone do not establish hepatic dysfunction.
